analysis: Integration review of the Flint paged-only PR. Production changes: (1) EngineV2KVQuantizationPolicy.swift:78-86 stops consulting the provider-wide `global` default for modelType flint. Env or per-model non-native selections still throw flintRequiresNative, and the result stays .native, so Flint never gets reduced KV or checkpoint precision implicitly. (2) EngineV2Factory+BackendPreparation.swift:180-183 promotes .auto to .paged for FlintModel, and lines 222-227 throw pagedUnavailable if resolvedKind != .paged. Together these are a fail-closed tightening: the crash-loop guard, kill switch, explicit contiguous selection and capability veto now refuse the load instead of serving contiguous. The cost is Flint availability, which is an intentional qualification choice and not attacker-reachable beyond the operator's own machine (ADV-001 only affects their own availability). (3) ModelBenchmarkNativeQwen4.swift:38-40 and ThroughputSweep.swift:123-132 and 203-209 are benchmark-only: they route Flint through the production CBv2 session and skip scalar prefill. Benchmark runs disable the prefix cache and create no at-rest artifact. The rest is docs, changelog and tests that assert the fail-closed behavior. No coordinator wire, attestation, App Attest, key custody or encryption paths are touched. T-041 (SSD prefix cache) is unchanged in HMAC naming, TTL, salt scoping and DBK3 format. Native checkpoint precision only keeps Flint on its existing posture. Unverified: the full prepareProductionBackend body between the override and the refusal check, whether any other Flint construction path in EngineV2SlotFactory bypasses the paged requirement (the new test at FlintContextAdmissionTests suggests it is covered), and that paged Flint serving preserves cacheSalt scoping. Replay was incomplete (50 units omitted), but no concrete regression is evidenced.
